title: Selecting comparable companies
objectives: Answer out loud: How do you choose comps?
Answer out loud: What if there aren't any?

blocks.body: Screen on: industry/business model, size (revenue, market cap), growth, margins, geography, and customer type. Aim for 5–10 good comps rather than 20 loose ones.

blocks.template: A typical comps set has about {{1}} companies
Comps are selected on business model, size, {{1}}, margins, and geography

blocks.title: What if there are no good comps?
blocks.teaser: Widen the criteria (adjacent industries, different geographies), weight the closest comps more heavily, lean more on the DCF, or use a sum-of-the-par…
blocks.body:
Widen the criteria (adjacent industries, different geographies), weight the closest comps more heavily, lean more on the DCF, or use a sum-of-the-parts with different comps for each segment.

**Interview answer:** "I'd widen the screen to adjacent businesses, lean more on the DCF, and be clear about which comps are closest."

blocks.title: Why isn't "same industry" enough?
blocks.teaser: A 30%-growth SaaS company and a 3%-growth legacy software company are both "software" but deserve very different multiples.
blocks.body: A 30%-growth SaaS company and a 3%-growth legacy software company are both "software" but deserve very different multiples. Business model, growth, and margins matter more than the label.

blocks.prompt: Two software companies: one growing 30%, one growing 3%. Should they trade at the same multiple?

options.text: Yes — same industry means same multiple
No — business model, growth and margins matter more than the industry label
Yes, as long as they're the same size
No — the slower grower should trade higher because it's safer

blocks.explanation: Comps need similar growth, margins and business model, not just the same label.

blocks.title: Should a small company be valued at the same multiple as large peers?
blocks.body: Often not. Smaller companies usually carry a discount for less liquidity, customer concentration, and higher risk.
